items.detail: Friday's bounce lasted exactly one session — the **S&P 500 fell 37.02 points (0.48%) to 7,619**, the **Dow dropped 152.01 points (0.29%) to 52,421** and the **Nasdaq lost 146.62 points (0.56%) to 26,186**, though all three closed well off their session lows.
items.why: Two separate shocks hit at once: frontier AI lab CEOs publicly called for slowing AI development, which gutted the semiconductor complex, while crude spiked to a four-month high and pushed the 10-year Treasury yield to 5%.

items.detail: The AI trade cracked from the inside — Anthropic CEO **Dario Amodei** published an essay calling for an industry-wide slowdown, **Sam Altman and Elon Musk agreed** and **Microsoft** endorsed a more prudent pace, sending **Micron down over 5%**, **Marvell nearly 6%**, **Intel and AMD 4% each** and **Nvidia about 3%**, with **SoftBank closing 11% lower in Japan**; Altman also told Fortune **OpenAI is delaying its IPO to 2027**.
items.why: If the labs themselves throttle development, the compute-spending assumption underwriting the entire AI capex rally gets smaller, so investors marked down the hardware suppliers furthest along that spending chain.

items.detail: The money that left chips went straight into cybersecurity — **CrowdStrike surged 15.25%** and **Palo Alto Networks rose 13.98%**, both up more than 13% on a day the Nasdaq fell, after CrowdStrike CEO George Kurtz argued frontier labs will keep building regardless and the security industry's job is to make that safer.
items.why: A slower, safety-first AI build-out reads as a spending increase rather than a cut for vendors selling AI risk mitigation, so the same headline that de-rated semis re-rated security software.

items.detail: Friday's de-escalation trade was fully reversed — **Brent jumped 3.56% to $108.34**, a four-month high, after Saudi Arabia confirmed the drone-hit **East–West pipeline will be out of service for weeks** (repair estimates run **five to six weeks**), stranding the roughly **5 million barrels a day** it was rerouting to Yanbu while the Strait of Hormuz stays closed.
items.why: Tehran postponed the GCC talks that had knocked $3 off Brent on Friday, and the pipeline outage removes the only working workaround to the Hormuz blockade — up to 4% of world supply — turning a war premium into an actual physical shortfall.

items.detail: The 10-year Treasury finally printed a 5-handle — the yield hit **5.01% intraday, the highest since October 2023**, before easing back to close around **4.96%**, extending Friday's front-end-led selloff into the long end.
items.why: Oil at a four-month high on a supply outage measured in weeks rather than headlines forces a higher inflation path into the term premium, not just into the next Fed meeting.

items.detail: The FOMC convenes today for a two-day meeting with a **25bp hike to 3.75%–4.00% priced at roughly 85%**, and the decision plus updated dot plot lands **Wednesday at 2:00pm ET** — while the White House keeps up an unusually public pressure campaign, Trump having threatened to **halt trade with deficit partners** unless the Fed cuts instead.
items.why: This would be the first Fed hike since 2023, and Chair Kevin Warsh — Trump's own appointee — has to deliver it against explicit presidential opposition, making the press conference a credibility test as much as a policy one.

items.detail: Dalal Street reopened with a gap-up after Monday's **Ganesh Chaturthi holiday** — the **Sensex opened 587.87 points (0.79%) higher at 75,369.63** and the **Nifty 50 began at 23,576.15, up 178.05 points (0.76%)**, with GIFT Nifty having signalled a positive start some 80 points above fair value.
items.why: A two-session break let buyers step into a market that had already shed almost 5% over five straight losing weeks, and firmer Asian cues including a 0.6% gain in the Nikkei outweighed a weak Wall Street close.

items.detail: India's own inflation test came back hot while the market was shut — **August CPI rose to 4.82% from 4.45% in July**, a **tenth consecutive monthly increase**, with **food inflation at 5.95%**, rural prices at **5.23%** against urban **4.31%**, and **personal care up 15.17%** and goods transport services up more than **14%**.
items.why: The Gulf energy shock is now feeding through India's cost structure via transport and input costs rather than just the fuel line, which is the leakage the RBI cannot treat as temporary even with the print still inside its 2–6% band.

items.detail: Wholesale prices confirmed the pipeline pressure — **August WPI inflation came in at 9.92%, up from 9.78% in July**, driven by **Fuel and Power at 22.93%** against 20.05% a month earlier, with Manufactured Products at **8.37%** even as Primary Articles cooled to **7.76%** from 8.52%.
items.why: Fuel is the single component accelerating, so the crude shock is still moving up the wholesale chain and has not yet been fully passed to consumers — which points to more, not less, retail inflation ahead.

items.detail: Final Friday flow data came in heavier than the provisional read — **FIIs net sold ₹930.90 crore** against **DII buying of ₹1,968 crore**, lifting September's foreign outflow to **₹13,138 crore** and the 2026 total to **₹2,37,579 crore**.
items.why: With a US hike all but certain on Wednesday and the rupee near record lows, the dollar-hedged return on Indian equities keeps shrinking, so foreign allocators continue trimming while domestic institutions absorb roughly two rupees for every one sold.

items.detail: The gap-up is fighting three headwinds at once — **Brent back near $107–108**, the **US 10-year at the 5% mark**, and a weak rupee, with the Saudi pipeline outage meaning India's import bill stays inflated for **weeks rather than days**; oil-sensitive sectors including aviation, paints, tyres and chemicals carry the direct margin hit.
items.why: India imports over 80% of its crude, so a supply outage with a five-to-six-week repair timeline converts directly into a wider current account deficit, more rupee pressure and higher input costs — the same loop that drove five straight weekly losses.

items.detail: Bitcoin ground higher through Monday rather than squeezing — it **opened at $76,806 and traded above $79,000**, with **Ether near $2,500**, **Solana around $101.92** and **XRP leading the broadest single-day advance in two weeks**, as **liquidations ran at roughly half Friday's pace**.
items.why: Unlike Friday's $424 million short-covering cascade, Monday's move came on a genuine spot bid with little forced buying, which is a structurally healthier advance even though it stopped short of $80,000.

items.detail: The rally has already given back most of its gains — **Bitcoin has slipped to about $77,800** after Monday's highs above $79,000, with oil's rebound to roughly **$103** adding to the inflation problem hours before the Fed is expected to lift the funds target to **3.75%–4.00%**.
items.why: Crypto is trading as a pure duration asset right now: a renewed oil-driven inflation impulse raises the discount rate applied to it, so the Saudi pipeline headline capped BTC in exactly the way it lifted Treasury yields.

items.detail: The CLARITY Act went to the wire — **Senate Democrats led by Ruben Gallego sent a counterproposal late Monday**, hours before today's **2:15pm ET cloture vote** that needs **60 votes**; the White House had already conceded new ethics language on Sunday, but the remaining objection is that it would still **block state attorneys general from bringing enforcement actions directly**. Polymarket now puts passage at about **18%**.
items.why: Republicans hold 53 seats and need at least seven Democrats, so a last-minute counteroffer on the ethics carve-out rather than an agreement means the sticking point is unresolved going into a vote that effectively decides the bill's fate for this Congress.

items.detail: The SEC pre-empted a failed vote — Chair **Paul Atkins backed the CLARITY Act** but said the agency **will keep pushing its own crypto rulemaking regardless of whether the bill passes**, while a **House panel released a crypto tax bill** ahead of a hearing later this week.
items.why: By decoupling the SEC's rule agenda from the legislative outcome, Atkins lowered the stakes of today's cloture vote for the industry's regulatory path even as it stays binary for the bill itself.

items.detail: The ETF story is a divergence, not a uniform exit — spot Bitcoin funds bled **$463 million** last week, ending a **three-week inflow streak**, led by **ARK 21Shares at $234.2 million**, **Grayscale's GBTC at $129.1 million**, **BlackRock's IBIT at $52.5 million** and **Fidelity's FBTC at $50.7 million**, while **spot Ether ETFs took in $197 million for a fourth straight week of inflows**.
items.why: Allocators are rotating within crypto rather than leaving it, trimming the macro-sensitive Bitcoin exposure into a likely hike while continuing to add Ether — which explains why Ether has outperformed on both Friday's squeeze and Monday's grind higher.

crossCuttingTheme: Friday's de-escalation trade was erased over the weekend when Saudi Arabia confirmed its drone-hit East–West pipeline — the only working workaround to Iran's Hormuz blockade, carrying about 5 million barrels a day — will be down for five to six weeks and Tehran postponed the GCC talks, turning a war premium into a physical shortfall that drove Brent up 3.56% to $108.34, pushed the US 10-year to 5.01% for the first time since October 2023, knocked the S&P 500 down 0.48% to 7,619, capped Bitcoin's $79,000 rally back at $77,800, and showed up directly in India's data with August CPI at 4.82% and WPI fuel inflation at 22.93% — so the same barrel of oil is now setting the Fed's Wednesday hike, the RBI's inflation path and crypto's discount rate simultaneously.
